transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Enterprise Finance - Head of ML), Aisha Patel (Platform Eng), Carlos Rivera (Security)

Summary: quick review of last week's bench results, decide which model to pin for production pilot, discuss rollback/fallback strategy and security checks. Agree next steps: share updated benchmark sheet, provision test keys, security review.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for making time, uh quick roll call?
[00:06] Liam: here, Liam.
[00:08] Aisha: Aisha here.
[00:10] Carlos: Carlos on security.
[00:12] Priya: Priya from Redwood. Jordan?
[00:15] Jordan: yep, Jordan. Alright cool, we're about 45 minutes. agenda: bench recap, model selection, pinning, rollback strategy, security open items.

[02:01] Priya: quick recap - we re-ran the latency bench with the two candidates we talked about: "rw-alpha-1.3" (larger) and "rw-beta-quant-v2" (quantized). results were P50 ~ 110ms vs 85ms, P95 420ms vs 260ms, cost delta about 40% lower for quant model but with slight drop in long-form coherence on a couple bank-specific prompts.

[03:20] Liam: mmh yeah we saw that in our eval set - customer-consent extraction had a few hallucinations on the quantized runs, like mixing account numbers across examples, so we're nervous about shipping that as-is.

[04:05] Jordan: totally expected. tradeoff is cost vs quality. for pilot we recommend pinning to the larger rw-alpha-1.3 for production traffic and keeping rw-beta-quant-v2 as a fallback for low-priority async jobs. pinning lets you lock the version across the route so no silent rollouts.

[04:48] Aisha: question, how hard is it to do an instantaneous rollback if we see regressions? say we deploy rw-alpha-1.3 and we see a spike in error rate or drift.

[05:02] Priya: good q. Redwood supports route-level version pinning and quick rollbacks - you can flip to a pinned previous model, or define a fallback policy to a smaller variant automatically. rollback is basically config and happens within seconds for hosted; for Dedicated we need the variant to be warmed (kv cache and batching warm-up) so there is a brief cold penalty.

[05:35] Carlos: what's the KV cache warm-up like? our concern is P95 spikes during a rollback window.

[05:42] Priya: yeah so KV cache and continuous batching are runtime artifacts - when you change models you lose the warm KV for long context. tradeoffs: cold-start P95 can double for first few hundred requests, then stabilize. mitigation: we can do staged canary with traffic shadowing and also pre-warm by replaying recent requests in a dry run.

[06:28] Liam: does Redwood offer an autoscale burst for Dedicated? we want predictable throughput but some spikes on month-end reports.

[06:36] Jordan: Dedicated supports burst capacity, you can configure autoscale policies, and we can set a cost cap. but bursts are billed separately. we'll include that in the cost sheet.

[07:10] Aisha: security-wise, Carlos had some questions about KMS and logs retention. Carlos?

[07:15] Carlos: yeah, couple items: 1) does Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM for key encryption? 2) can we get field-level audit logs and long-term retention to satisfy SOX/SOC2? 3) SSO using our Okta SAML - do you support SCIM for provisioning?

[07:38] Priya: yes on KMS/HSM in Private deployments, for Hosted we integrate with customer KMS via a linked account in Dedicated/Private. audit logs are available; retention is configurable as an add-on. we support SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning. I'll attach the SOC2 package and KMS integration notes after the call.

[08:05] Carlos: ok, please include any limitations around exportability of logs and how keys rotate.

[08:18] Jordan: will do.

[09:00] Priya: back to models - we sketched a fallback matrix: route pinned -> primary rw-alpha-1.3, fallback rw-beta-quant-v2, secondary fallback to rw-small-1 if both fail to keep latencies stable. fallback policy can be based on model errors or latency SLO breaches. we'll share the matrix.

[10:22] Liam: would prefer fewer variants; ops overhead grows with each extra model. can we instead use quantization profiles for rw-alpha-1.3?

[10:30] Priya: there are quant profiles we can produce that keep more FP fidelity for critical tokens; smaller perf hit but better quality than full quant. it's a middle ground - we recommend testing that on your prompt set.

[11:12] Aisha: what's the telemetry we get for rollouts? need per-route P50/P95, token counts, model version, and sample outputs for any regression alert.

[11:20] Jordan: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route latencies, trace IDs, and you can attach a few logged samples when alerts fire. we can also set automatic rollback when quality regressions exceed threshold tied to your eval set.

[12:05] Carlos: alerting hooks - do you integrate with PagerDuty and our internal Slack?

[12:10] Priya: yes, webhooks, PagerDuty, Slack integrations are supported.

[13:00] Liam: ok on the bench details - Jordan, can you walk through a few concrete examples where quant model failed?

[13:08] Jordan: sure - on prompt set A (account summary extraction) the quant model misattributed balances across statements in 4/100 samples; on prompt set B (customer intent classification) it was fine. so it's very prompt-dependent. we annotated the failing examples in the spreadsheet.

[15:20] Aisha: what's the plan for canaries? we want a canary window for at least 24 hours with 5-10% traffic, and shadowing for full traffic to collect samples.

[15:35] Priya: recommended plan: 1) start with 5% canary pinned to rw-alpha-1.3, 2) shadow 100% to rw-beta-quant-v2 to collect async samples, 3) after 24-48h, increase canary if no regressions, 4) have automatic rollback on specific failure signals.

[16:45] Carlos: two security caveats - for shadowing, ensure no PII leaves your systems in logs unless redacted; also verify retention policy on shadow outputs.

[17:02] Jordan: noted. we'll mask PII and we can filter logged samples.

[18:30] Liam: on performance testing - can we run end-to-end P95 under expected load? we want numbers with real payloads, not synthetic.

[18:40] Priya: absolutely. Priya will provision a small Dedicated pool and you can run weekend load tests. that will surface batching behavior and P95 under true request mixes.

[19:05] Priya: small note on cost math - quant model saved ~40% per-token in our tests, but after accounting for increased error-handling and human review that may erode benefits. that's why pilot metrics are key.

[20:10] Aisha: what's the recommended pin for pilot then?

[20:15] Jordan: recommendation: pin rw-alpha-1.3 for the primary production route; set rw-beta-quant-v2 as a fallback for background jobs and for a shadowed experiment. also run a quantized profile of rw-alpha-1.3 on a sample subset. That gives safety and cost experiments.

[22:00] Liam: timeline? we'd like to be in pilot prod next week if security sign-off is quick.

[22:10] Carlos: security needs 3 days to review docs once we get them.

[22:18] Jordan: we'll aim to get docs by EOB tomorrow.

[23:30] Priya: operational detail - when we pin a version in the Redwood Console, it's a strong pin; you can still configure fallback policies. also you can tag routes with risk levels and require approval before rollouts.

[24:20] Aisha: any gotchas around streaming or function calls? our flows rely on partial responses to show progress.

[24:30] Priya: streaming behavior is preserved across model variants but quantization can affect tokenization edge cases; we recommend testing streaming scenarios during the weekend run.

[26:00] Liam: let's talk about rollback SLOs - we need rollback to mitigate customer-facing errors within 15 minutes ideally. is that achievable?

[26:10] Priya: for hosted routes yes, for Dedicated we can get close but need pre-warmed variants; otherwise expect a brief spike. we recommend the canary approach and monitored auto-rollback to meet the 15-minute objective.

[27:50] Carlos: on encryption key rotation, is there an automated process or manual?

[28:00] Jordan: rotation is supported and can be automated; for Private you control rotation schedules in your KMS. we'll document the exact steps.

[29:45] Liam: ok what about cost allocation tags? we need per-team tagging so we can bill back.

[29:52] Priya: you can add tags per route/model invocation; Console and billing exports will include tags for chargebacks.

[31:10] Jordan: quick callouts from last week's bench - attached spreadsheet has annotated fails, a cost sheet with Dedicated vs Hosted, and a proposed pinning/fallback matrix. Jordan: action item to update the sheet with burst pricing and autoscale assumptions.

[33:00] Aisha: can you include quantization profile results for rw-alpha-1.3 in next sheet?

[33:05] Priya: yes we'll add a quant-profile run.

[34:20] Liam: ok agreed plan - pin rw-alpha-1.3 for the route, fallback to rw-beta-quant-v2 for async, run weekend Dedicated P95 load tests, security to review SOC2/KMS docs, and Jordan to update bench file.

[35:00] Jordan: recap of next steps: share updated benchmark + fallback matrix (Jordan), provision test Dedicated and credentials (Priya), customer to upload prompt sets and pass/fail (Liam), security review (Carlos).

[36:10] Carlos: please include the exact S3 bucket retention, encryption-at-rest metadata in docs.

[36:20] Jordan: will include.

[37:00] Aisha: one minor ask - can we have a daily small report during the 48h canary that includes top-5 regression samples?

[37:10] Priya: yes we can configure daily digest and push to a shared Slack channel or S3.

[38:40] Liam: anything else?

[38:45] Jordan: nothing major. thanks all. we'll follow up via shared drive.

[39:00] End recap and explicit next steps repeated.

Recorded artifacts referenced: link: /shared/benchmarks/ENTF-pilot-2027-11.xlsx (bench sheet), /docs/security/SOC2-Redwood-2027.pdf (SOC2), /docs/integration/kms-integration-notes.md

Notes about transcript: automated transcription, occasional mis-heard words; speaker turns approximated.

COACH: final recap - Pilot plan for next week: pin rw-alpha-1.3, fallback to quantized variant, run Dedicated weekend load tests, update bench sheet, security review.
